title: Grade 6 Science — Mon, Jun 16
description: Changes Around Us — Day 1 of 5: Physical vs chemical changes
subject: science

questions.question: A physical change is one in which ___.
options: The composition of the substance changes
Only the form or appearance changes
questions.explanation: In a physical change, only form, shape, size, or state changes. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: A chemical change always produces ___.
options: One or more new substances with different properties
questions.explanation: A chemical change produces new substances with different properties from the original substances.

questions.question: Melting of ice is a ___.
questions.explanation: Melting of ice is a physical change — water changes from solid to liquid state. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: Burning of paper is a ___.
questions.explanation: Burning paper is a chemical change — it produces ash and gases (new substances) and cannot be reversed.

questions.question: Which of these is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change — the salt can be recovered by evaporation. No new substance is formed.

questions.question: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron is a chemical change — iron reacts with water and oxygen to form iron oxide (rust), a new substance.

questions.question: In which type of change is the original substance generally NOT recoverable?
questions.explanation: Chemical changes are generally irreversible — the original substances cannot easily be recovered.

questions.question: Folding a piece of paper is an example of a ___.
questions.explanation: Folding only changes the shape — no new substance is formed. It is a physical change.

questions.question: Formation of curd from milk is a ___.
questions.explanation: Curdling of milk is a chemical change — bacteria convert lactose to lactic acid, forming curd (a new substance).

questions.question: One sign that a chemical change has occurred is ___.
options: Formation of gas, new colour, or new smell
questions.explanation: Chemical changes are often indicated by gas production, colour change, smell, heat/light, or formation of a precipitate.

questions.question: Tearing paper into pieces is a ___.
questions.explanation: Tearing only changes the size and shape — the paper remains paper. It is a physical change.

questions.question: Cooking food is a ___.
questions.explanation: Cooking involves chemical reactions that change the composition of food — new substances are formed.

questions.question: Evaporation of water is a ___.
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a physical change — water changes from liquid to vapour, but remains water (no new substance).

questions.question: Which property MOST clearly identifies a chemical change?
questions.explanation: The hallmark of a chemical change is the formation of one or more new substances with different properties.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs are BOTH chemical changes?
questions.explanation: Both burning wood and rusting iron produce new substances → both are chemical changes.
